jobs.title: Deputy Director of Emergency Services
jobs.description:
Description

Under general direction of the Director of Emergency Services, assists in planning, directing, coordinating, and managing the programs and operations of Ventura County Sheriff Emergency Services. Serves as a principal advisor to the Director on emergency management matters and provides leadership for disaster preparedness, mitigation, response, recovery, homeland security, continuity planning, emergency communications, and Operational Area coordination activities. Exercises direct supervision over professional, technical, administrative, and support staff.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

The Deputy Director of Emergency Services is a management-level classification responsible for assisting in the administration of countywide emergency management programs and services. The incumbent may act on behalf of the Director of Emergency Services in their absence and serve in a key leadership role during emergencies, disasters, and Emergency Operations Center activations.

The Deputy Director of Emergency Services is expected to function as an emergency management executive and operational leader during disasters and major incidents. The incumbent routinely serves in emergency response and coordination roles, including participation in the Department's Duty Officer Program, Emergency Operations Center activations, Operational Area coordination activities, and field response operations.

PAYROLL TITLE:
Sheriff's Senior Manager II

AGENCY/DEPARTMENT:
Sheriff / Office of Emergency Services

Ventura County offers an excellent benefit package. F or more details regarding the benefits offered by Ventura County click here: https://hr.ventura.org/benefits .

Sheriff's Senior Manager II is a Management/Confidential classification and is not eligible for overtime compensation. Incumbents in this classification are eligible for benefits at the MB3 level.

The eligible list established from this recruitment may be used to fill present and future regular, temporary, fixed-term, intermittent, and extra-help vacancies for this position only
. There is currently one (1) Regular vacancy within the Sheriff's Office.

TENTATIVE SCHEDULE

OPENING DATE:
Monday, August 24, 2026

CLOSING DATE:
Continuous and may close at any time; therefore, the schedule for the remainder of the process will depend upon when a sufficient number of qualified applications are received to meet business needs.

Examples Of Duties

Duties may include but are not limited to the following:

Assists in directing and managing Ventura County's comprehensive emergency management program, including mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience initiatives.
Acts on behalf of the Director of Emergency Services as assigned.
Supervises professional, technical, administrative, and support staff engaged in emergency management and homeland security activities.
Assists in the development, implementation, evaluation, and maintenance of countywide emergency management policies, procedures, plans, and programs, including the Operational Area Emergency Operations Plan, hazard mitigation plans, evacuation plans, continuity plans, recovery frameworks, and related emergency management documents.
Coordinates Operational Area emergency management activities, mutual aid operations, and preparedness, response, recovery, and mitigation efforts with local governments, special districts, tribal governments, state and federal agencies, non-governmental organizations, and private sector partners.
Provides technical guidance and policy recommendations regarding emergency management laws, regulations, standards, and best practices.
Represents Ventura County Sheriff Emergency Services on local, regional, state, and federal committees, working groups, and task forces.
Assists in administering homeland security, emergency management, hazard mitigation, and disaster recovery grants and related funding programs.
Assists with contract administration, procurement activities, and vendor management related to emergency management programs and projects.
Develops reports, presentations, grant applications, funding requests, and policy recommendations for executive leadership, elected officials, and external partners.
Assists in the administration of public warning and emergency notification systems, emergency communications programs, and situational awareness initiatives.
Oversees or coordinates emergency management training, exercises, and corrective action programs.
Responds to emergencies and disasters; oversees or participates in Emergency Operations Center activations and incident management activities; serves in Incident Command System and Emergency Operations Center leadership positions; and provides operational coordination and leadership during extended emergency operations, disaster response, and recovery activities.
Participates in the Ventura County Sheriff Emergency Services Duty Officer Program, providing after-hours emergency management coordination, situational awareness, incident support, and response to emergencies, disasters, and other significant incidents.
Other duties as assigned.

Typical Qualifications

These are entrance requirements to the examination process and assures neither continuance in the process nor placement on an eligible list.

Education And Experience

Any combination of education, training, and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities. Typical qualifying experience would include:

A Bachelor's degree in Emergency Management, Public Administration, Homeland Security, Business Administration, or a closely related field; AND three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in emergency management, public safety, homeland security, disaster recovery, mass care and sheltering, or related governmental/military operations. This experience must include at least two (2) years of experience exercising operational leadership within an emergency management, public safety, or disaster response environment (such as serving as a supervisor, programmatic lead, shift commander, or in an Emergency Operations Center [EOC] leadership capacity).

OR

Seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in emergency management, public safety, homeland security, disaster recovery, mass care and sheltering, or related governmental/military operations. This experience must include at least two (2) years of experience exercising operational leadership within an emergency management, public safety, or disaster response environment (such as serving as a supervisor, programmatic lead, shift commander, or in an Emergency Operations Center [EOC] leadership capacity).

Necessary Special Requirements

Licensing: Ability to obtain and maintain a valid California Class C driver's license.
Background: Must successfully pass and complete a comprehensive background investigation.
On-Call Availability: Must participate in a rotating on-call Duty Officer Program and be available for emergency response outside of normal working hours.
Disaster Response: Availability to respond to incident scenes, Emergency Operations Center (EOC) activations, and emergency assignments throughout Ventura County on a 24-hour basis.
Extended Operations: Ability and willingness to work extended hours, including evenings, weekends, holidays, overnight operations, and multi-day activations during emergencies, disasters, and other significant incidents.
Crisis Leadership: Ability to serve effectively in EOC leadership positions, Incident Command System (ICS) assignments, Operational Area coordination roles, or other emergency management functions during active disasters.

Desired

Experience working with local, state, and federal elected officials and government agencies. Demonstrated understanding of governmental processes, public policy, and the ability to effectively navigate complex political and intergovernmental environments is highly desirable.
Progressively responsible experience in local or county emergency management programs, including coordination of multi-agency emergency operations, and collaboration with public safety agencies, government partners, and community stakeholders. Experience leading or supporting Emergency Operations (EOC) activations and implementing SEMS, NIMS, and ICS principles is highly desirable.
Experience in developing and implementing disaster preparedness training and exercises.
Experience in obtaining and/or administering state and federal grant programs, including FEMA Public Assistance, FEMA Individual Assistance and California Disaster Assistance Act program.
Possession of, or the ability to obtain, appropriate emergency management professional certifications (e.g., CSTI or FEMA credentials) within a designated timeframe.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Thorough knowledge of: Principles and practices of emergency management, homeland security, and public administration; The California Emergency Services Act, Standardized Emergency Management System (SEMS), National Incident Management System (NIMS), and Incident Command System (ICS); Emergency planning, disaster response, disaster recovery, hazard mitigation, and continuity planning principles; Grant administration and public-sector budgeting practices; Personnel management, supervision, employee development, and performance evaluation; Principles of intergovernmental relations and collaborative problem-solving; Emergency notification, public warning, and emergency communications systems.

Ability to: Plan, organize, direct, and evaluate complex emergency management programs; Effectively supervise, train, motivate, and evaluate subordinate staff; Establish and maintain effective working relationships with elected officials, department heads, city managers, public safety executives, community organizations, and members of the public; Analyze complex problems and develop practical solutions; Prepare and present clear and concise reports, recommendations, and policy analyses; Communicate effectively both orally and in writing; Lead emergency operations under stressful and rapidly changing conditions; Interpret and apply laws, regulations, policies, and technical guidance related to emergency management.

Job Description

The Position:

The Chief, Transformation and Strategic Initiatives Branch , plays a pivotal role in driving UNFPA’s institutional transformation and strategic positioning, acting as a key partner to the Chief of Staff in advancing organization-wide reform, innovation, and performance. The role serves as a central integrator of cross-organizational transformation efforts, including UNFPA’s change management and transformation processes, broader UN80 reform processes, and priority corporate initiatives

The position of Chief, Transformation and Strategic Initiatives Branch, is located within the Office of the Executive Director, and reports to the Chief of Staff, working closely with the Chief of Staff to drive institutional priorities and ensure coherence across strategic, operational, and reform agendas

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person's potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

In supervision of the team, the Chief will empower UNFPA through expert guidance, strategic coordination, capacity building and knowledge management, fostering a dynamic environment where transformation and strategic and innovative initiatives thrives. By forging strategic partnerships across sectors, the Chief will mobilize expertise, capabilities and resources to advance priority initiatives,, accelerating progress towards the three transformative results. The key priorities of this position are:

Lead and support institutional transformation and organizational change: Design coordinate and advance selected transformation and change initiatives,, ensuring coherence with with organizational priorities reform processes and emerging trends.
Advance strategic and innovative initiatives: : Support the development, incubation and acceleration of selected strategic and innovative initiatives aligned with organizational goals, priorities, emerging opportunities, and insights from foresight activities.
Foster an enabling environment for transformation: Build capacity, enable knowledge sharing, and support organizational learning to advance transformation, strategic initiatives and organizational effectiveness in line with broader UN processes and organizational transformation processes, including UN80 initiatives, as appropriate.
Enable strategic partnerships and new approaches: : Forge partnerships and facilitate access to relevant expertise, technologies and financing approaches to support transformation priorities and strategic initiatives, in coordination with relevant organizational units.

Lead and Coordinate Institutional Transformation and Strategic Initiatives
Lead the management, strategic planning and coordination of selected institutional transformation priorities and strategic initiatives to support leadership with priority-setting, forward planning and strategic analysis.
Lead and coordinate with UNFPA Business Units efforts to design and mobilize transformation approaches and strategic and innovative initiatives, and guide and oversee their implementation, ensuring coherence with organizational priorities, Strategic Plans, UN Reforms, and emerging trends.
Provide strategic leadership and stewardship for for UNFPA's transformation and strategic innovation agenda ,, ensuring alignment with the Strategic Plan, organizational goals, and insights from foresight activities to advance corporate performance.
Ensure alignment of transformation priorities and strategic initiatives with executive decision-making processes, including direct support to the Executive Committee and senior leadership forums,.
Ensure harmonization and linkages with institutional messaging oninstitutional transformation, strategic initiatives and innovation in interactions with the Member States, UN inter-agency groups, donors and other partners.
Lead or provide strategic coordination and acceleration support to selected high-priority transformation and strategic initiatives, ensuring delivery of results across business units including special corporate or change management projects including projects/initiatives relating to innovation and transformation.
Act as a central coordination point across divisions, regions, and governance bodies to ensure alignment and execution of selected transformation priorities and strategic initiatives under the Branch’s remit..
Enable Organizational Learning and Transformation Capacity
Deliver learning opportunities on transformation, change and strategic initiatives and support building capacity of Business Units for these efforts.
Ensure availability of technical assistance, best practices, tools, and methods for transformation and strategic and innovative initiatives empowering teams to overcome challenges and achieve progress.

Facilitate communities of practice and knowledge exchange on transformation, innovation and strategic initiatives, as relevant..
Develop and curate knowledge resources on innovation and corporate performance optimization, fostering information exchange within and beyond UNFPA.
Provide operational support for both innovation and corporate performance initiatives, streamlining processes and systems to support efficient implementation.

Champion initiatives that foster collaboration across Business Units and external actors, building synergies and maximizing impact to advance organizational priorities.

Identify and cultivate new models of partnership that leverage complementary capabilities across sectors, considering how these partnerships can enable transformation and strategic initiatives..

Provide specialist advice and support to develop partnership and financing approaches for strategic initiatives, in coordination with relevant organizational units.

Braven is a national nonprofit that prepares promising college students to secure a strong first opportunity after college graduation through a career-accelerating program.

About The Role

In order to achieve its ambition of serving 80,000-100,000 Fellows over the next decade, Braven is hiring an Executive Director (ED) in North Carolina (NC). This person will lead our efforts to launch and oversee Braven's potential new NC region, including its first potential new higher education partner within NC. The ED will also work with the Central External Affairs team and the future NC External Affairs Director to raise roughly $9M for the first three years of programming before the launch of the new school site, among other external priorities.

Should a partnership with a higher education institution in the NC solidify, this temporary position would become a permanent full-time regional role, leading the NC team as the region's most senior-level executive and the face of Braven. They will be responsible for all major outcomes in the region and set the vision and direction for how Braven comes alive successfully in their region. They build and lead the regional program team and a regional advisory board, guide expansion decisions alongside their regional board, manage their External Affairs Director and lead their External Affairs strategy in close collaboration with the central External Affairs team, serve as a Braven organizational leader on the Alignment Team (AT) and ensure they and Braven are the primary thought leaders in the college-to-career space in their region.

The ED will initially report to the Chief of Regional Success and Innovation and ultimately transition to report to the Founder & CEO and be part of Braven's Alignment Team (AT), the organization's leadership body.

With the Regional Senior Director, ensuring strong program execution resulting in both positive experiences and outcomes for Fellows, volunteers, and partners

Focusing on significantly growing and diversifying a sustainable funding base that will include gifts from individuals, corporations, foundations, and government

Serving as the model and leader of Braven culture within the hub
Serving on the organization's Alignment Team to influence organization-wide impact, growth, and sustainability

Preferred Qualifications

Experience that has informed your belief in Braven's mission and has prepared you to work with or for Braven's student Fellow population

Performance Task

Braven offers competitive base salaries based on the midpoint of the market among not-for-profit organizations of similar size, with opportunities for salary growth over time. We believe in compensating staff members fairly in relation to each other, their qualifications, and their impact on behalf of the organization, and take internal and external equity seriously. Given our commitment to equity, Braven does not negotiate salary offers; instead, each salary offer is determined carefully using external and internal benchmarking.

Starting salary within the range is determined by role scope and qualifications, with new hires starting at the lower end to allow for growth with performance. The salary range for this role is $179,600-$224,400 with new hires starting at the beginning of the range to allow for room for growth. This is based on a 50-hour work week. This is a full-time, regular, exempt, and benefits eligible position where you will be working at 100% capacity.

We gather in the office at least 3 days per week (on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and often work remotely 2 days per week (although certain commitments might adjust that from time to time). The Executive Director (ED)
serves as the leader of the community, overseeing all day-to-day operations and ensuring residents are receiving exceptional care and service. Our EDs are the leaders of our Waltonwood communities, working each day to cultivate a community where our residents and associates can grow and thrive, developing bonds and memories that will last a lifetime.

The Administrative Department is the backbone of the community, ensuring day to day operations are running smoothly and that our residents are happy and safe in their homes. They work closely with all departments in the community, advocate on behalf of the residents, and solve any problems that arise. Staying upbeat and positive, exhibiting dedicated customer service and teamwork, and executing follow-through are critical to meeting the needs of our residents.

Oversee the daily operations of all community departments, working closely with community department heads to ensure resident, family, and associate satisfaction.
Lead and manage the community department heads and fill in for open department head positions whenever needed. Empower and support the leadership team with recruitment and retention efforts, onboarding and orientation of new associates, ensure adequate staffing, and performance management in all areas of the community.
Continuously motivate associates throughout the community to perform at a high level.
Work collaboratively with stakeholders throughout the company, including the Regional Director of Operations and members of the regional support team, on total quality management.
Meet personally with community residents and families to discuss and/or resolve customer concerns/comments/preferences.
Maintain and ensure ongoing compliance with all state, local and federal regulations.
Prepare budgets and manage revenue, net operating income, and other key performance indicators. Provide reports on occupancy, community financial performance, and other key indicators.
Act as a sales leader in the community, reviewing sales strategies with the marketing team, as well as providing community tours and building rapport with current and prospective residents daily.
Maintain the property to our highest standards, including ensuring apartments are move-in ready by addressing issues head on.
Work within and ensure and ensure Department Head leaders are using various systems and software including (but not limited to) property management software, payroll software, talent management systems, and associate scheduling software.
Assist with all other duties as assigned by the Regional Director of Operations.

At Waltonwood, we are all a part of a team who are here to serve the residents living in our communities. Our residents count on us every hour of every day. As such, we expect all associates and Department Heads alike to be willing to lend a helping hand to co-workers, direct reports, and supervisors, whether it is in their specific department or another unrelated to their day-to-day responsibilities. Department Heads need to keep the best interests of the residents and other associates in mind, and be an active participant in accomplishing team, community, and company goals. We expect our leaders to lead by example, demonstrate integrity and character, lead innovation and change, while inspiring and developing associates throughout the organization.

Passion for Seniors – Feels strongly about working with the senior population. Has a drive to go above and beyond for seniors. Typically, this comes from a personal experience or prior work experience in a senior citizen setting.

Integrity and Trust – Does what they say they will do, does not take the easy road, and does not misrepresent themselves for personal gain. Always does the right thing, even when it does not benefit themselves directly.

Certified Assisted Living Director, or equivalent (based on state certifications and requirements)
Excellent time management skills and ability to multi-task and stay organized.

Develop and implement Eco-Cycle’s fundraising strategy, in close coordination with the Executive Director and Board Development Committee:

Write grants, or support writing of grants by department directors

Write or assist with grant reports and ensure timely submission of reports

Capital campaign and event coordination experience a plus

The ED will also work with the Central External Affairs team and the future NC External Affairs Director to raise roughly $9M for the first three years of programming before the launch of the new school site, among other external priorities.

Should a partnership with a higher education institution in the NC solidify, this temporary position would become a permanent full-time regional role, leading the NC team as the region's most senior-level executive and the face of Braven. They will be responsible for all major outcomes in the region and set the vision and direction for how Braven comes alive successfully in their region. They build and lead the regional program team and a regional advisory board, guide expansion decisions alongside their regional board, manage their External Affairs Director and lead their External Affairs strategy in close collaboration with the central External Affairs team, serve as a Braven organizational leader on the Alignment Team (AT) and ensure they and Braven are the primary thought leaders in the college-to-career space in their region.

The ED will initially report to the Chief of Regional Success and Innovation and ultimately transition to report to the Founder & CEO and be part of Braven's Alignment Team (AT), the organization's leadership body.

What You'll Do

Regional Strategy and Operations (20%)

Implementing a comprehensive multi-year strategic plan to reach our vision for scale and excellent outcomes with our prospective partner and future NC region, higher education partners
With the Regional Senior Director, ensuring strong program execution resulting in both positive experiences and outcomes for Fellows, volunteers, and partners
Building, managing, and expanding a regional advisory board that will help maximize the NC region's impact, narrative, and sustainability

Stakeholder Management and Awareness Building (30%)

Ensuring the health of key stakeholder relationships at both university and employer partners, including university and corporate executives
Raising Braven's brand awareness through thought-leadership, awards, public speaking, social media, and press pieces
Explore the local political landscape and engage in critical policy efforts when relevant

Regional Fundraising and Sustainability (30%)

Raising roughly $9M prior to the launch of the new school, among other external priorities
Deepening our political capital and thought leadership to ensure that our region maintains its meaningful position in the educational fabric of the community
Focusing on significantly growing and diversifying a sustainable funding base that will include gifts from individuals, corporations, foundations, and government

Team Leadership and Management (20%)

Attracting, hiring, and developing a team of diverse and talented staff members
Directly manage and develop the Regional Senior Director and Director, External Affairs
Coaching and developing regional staff members to exhibit strong cultural leadership skills and orientations
Serving as the model and leader of Braven culture within the hub
Serving on the organization's Alignment Team to influence organization-wide impact, growth, and sustainability

Requirements

Minimum Requirements

BS/BA
7-10 years leadership experience as an Executive, leading a department, or similar, with a verifiable track record of achieving successful outcomes while maintaining an inclusive, equitable, and sustainable team culture

Preferred Qualifications

1-3 years in non-profit, higher education, economic or workforce development, or a chamber of commerce
Proficiency in Google Suite, Slack, Asana, Salesforce, Jira, Confluence
You have a demonstrated commitment to and understanding of the experiences of first-generation college students and students from low income backgrounds
You exemplify Braven's core values
Your experiences have informed your belief in Braven's mission and have prepared you to work with or for Braven's student Fellow population
Motivation and drive to fundraise and ensure the financial sustainability of the region; an ability to mobilize people and to create champions of an organizational mission
Experience building and working in partnership with partner organizations, funders, a Board of Directors, and other key constituents
Strong presence, communication skills, relationship-building skills, and maturity that engender respect and facilitate a strong partnership with very senior-level staff and Faculty, high-profile community stakeholders and civic leaders, Braven staff, Fellows, and Leadership Coaches
High level of personal responsibility, professional maturity and humility, commitment to personal growth, and self-awareness of one's own leadership style and its impact on others

Experience that has informed your belief in Braven's mission and has prepared you to work with or for Braven's student Fellow population

Work Demands

Ability to work in person in Fayetteville or Raleigh 3 days per week, depending on where the regional office is ultimately situated
Ability to travel in the NC region, especially Fayetteville, Raleigh, and Charlotte, regularly
Ability to travel to Braven hub cities across the country, and especially in Chicago, for meetings and events at least once a month

Additional Requirements

Authorized to work in the U.S

Application & Interview Process

Phone screen with Talent Team member

Performance Task
Panel Interview with Senior Braven Staff
In-Person Interview with Founder/CEO, Chief External Affairs Officer, and Chief Higher Ed Officer
Reference Checks
Panel Interviews with Braven Board members and regional stakeholders

Benefits

Compensation and Benefits

Braven offers competitive base salaries based on the midpoint of the market among not-for-profit organizations of similar size, with opportunities for salary growth over time. We believe in compensating staff members fairly in relation to each other, their qualifications, and their impact on behalf of the organization, and take internal and external equity seriously. Given our commitment to equity, Braven does not negotiate salary offers; instead, each salary offer is determined carefully using external and internal benchmarking.

Starting salary within the range is determined by role scope and qualifications, with new hires starting at the lower end to allow for growth with performance. Braven does not base compensation on individual candidate salary expectations and is committed to maintaining internal equity. The salary ranges are set by geographic market. The salary range for this role is $179,600-$224,400 with new hires starting at the beginning of the range to allow for room for growth. This is based on a 50-hour work week. Braven also provides a comprehensive total rewards package, recognition, and career development. While Braven reserves the right to change benefits at any time, current benefits include:

We gather in the office at least 3 days per week (on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and often work remotely 2 days per week (although certain commitments might adjust that from time to time). About TNFC

The New Foster Care’s (TNFC) is a 501c (3) non-profit organization based out of Oakland County. Founded in 2016, TNFC is a faith-based organization committed to making transformative changes within the Michigan foster care system creating a measurable, and meaningful impact in the lives of youth in and aging out of foster care.

TNFC serves people ages 14-29 through its Bridge Program, a comprehensive transitional support model that centers the young person as the driver of their own plan. Participants work with a Transition Navigator, Peer Support Specialist, Personal Wellness Coach, and Attorney to address any issues hindering their progress and develop a strategy for success across six life domains: Education, Employment, Housing, Transportation, Mental & Physical Health, and Community Connection.

Our work is grounded in relationship-based, trauma-informed, and strengths-focused practice,
delivered through an integrated multidisciplinary team.

The Program Director serves as a senior organizational leader responsible for advancing The New Foster Care's mission by providing strategic, operational, and hands-on leadership across the Bridge Program.

The ideal candidate is an innovative, servant leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is equally comfortable providing executive leadership, mentoring staff, solving complex operational challenges, nurturing community partnerships, and engaging directly with participants and multidisciplinary teams across the organization. This individual demonstrates exceptional emotional intelligence, strategic thinking, operational discipline, and an unwavering commitment to transforming outcomes for youth impacted by foster care.

The Program Director has a deep passion for the population served, and embraces a visionary approach to wraparound support while maintaining fidelity to TNFC’s participant-centered model.

Organizational Leadership & Operations
Provide strategic and operational leadership across the Bridge program, ensuring alignment with the mission, vision, and -organization priorities.
Lead, mentor, and develop department leaders and multidisciplinary teams by providing coaching, strategic guidance and support on complex cases, crisis response, staff development, organizational planning, and service delivery.
Maintain an engaged presence within program operations, building relationships with staff, participants, and community partners as needed.

Coordinate and facilitate relevant staff training and professional development opportunities that strengthen employee performance and organizational capacity.
Partner with leadership to ensure responsible fiscal stewardship through effective budget oversight, resource allocation, participant assistance funding, and long-term organizational sustainability.
Promote collaboration across all departments to ensure integrated, participant-centered service delivery and organizational alignment.

Cultivate and maintain strategic partnerships within the mental health, education, healthcare, and social services fields to advance TNFC's mission and strategic objectives.
Support grant development, contract procurement, fundraising initiatives, and sustainability efforts.
Coordinate all necessary program documentation, reports, and analyses as required for state appropriations, grants, and other funding sources.

Documentation & Compliance
Ensure program documentation, participant records, and outcome data are maintained accurately, timely, and in compliance with organizational, contractual, and regulatory requirements within Salesforce and the electronic medical record (EMR).
Design and implement program procedures to ensure staff comply with all relevant legislation, professional standards, and organization policies and procedures, up to and including:
HIPAA and all applicable confidentiality requirements governing client records and protected health information
Public and private funder and contract requirements

Apply knowledge of human development, behavioral health, trauma-informed

care, and strengths-based practices to leadership and participant-centered service delivery.

Experience managing multi-county or multi-site programs strongly preferred.

The Executive Director (ED)
serves as the leader of the community, overseeing all day-to-day operations and ensuring residents are receiving exceptional care and service. The ED thrives on providing a high level of customer service and leading a strong team of department heads. It is the responsibility of the ED to coordinate all of the moving parts of the community to deliver the best possible experience to all of its residents. This position reports to the Regional Director of Operations and is part of the Administrative team. Our EDs are the leaders of our Waltonwood communities, working each day to cultivate a community where our residents and associates can grow and thrive, developing bonds and memories that will last a lifetime.

The Administrative Department is the backbone of the community, ensuring day to day operations are running smoothly and that our residents are happy and safe in their homes. They work closely with all departments in the community, advocate on behalf of the residents, and solve any problems that arise. Staying upbeat and positive, exhibiting dedicated customer service and teamwork, and executing follow-through are critical to meeting the needs of our residents.

Lead and manage the community department heads and fill in for open department head positions whenever needed. Empower and support the leadership team with recruitment and retention efforts, onboarding and orientation of new associates, ensure adequate staffing, and performance management in all areas of the community.
Continuously motivate associates throughout the community to perform at a high level.
Work collaboratively with stakeholders throughout the company, including the Regional Director of Operations and members of the regional support team, on total quality management.
Meet personally with community residents and families to discuss and/or resolve customer concerns/comments/preferences.
Maintain and ensure ongoing compliance with all state, local and federal regulations.
Prepare budgets and manage revenue, net operating income, and other key performance indicators. Provide reports on occupancy, community financial performance, and other key indicators.
Act as a sales leader in the community, reviewing sales strategies with the marketing team, as well as providing community tours and building rapport with current and prospective residents daily.
Maintain the property to our highest standards, including ensuring apartments are move-in ready by addressing issues head on.
Work within and ensure and ensure Department Head leaders are using various systems and software including (but not limited to) property management software, payroll software, talent management systems, and associate scheduling software.
Assist with all other duties as assigned by the Regional Director of Operations.

At Waltonwood, we are all a part of a team who are here to serve the residents living in our communities. Our residents count on us every hour of every day. As such, we expect all associates and Department Heads alike to be willing to lend a helping hand to co-workers, direct reports, and supervisors, whether it is in their specific department or another unrelated to their day-to-day responsibilities. Department Heads need to keep the best interests of the residents and other associates in mind, and be an active participant in accomplishing team, community, and company goals. We expect our leaders to lead by example, demonstrate integrity and character, lead innovation and change, while inspiring and developing associates throughout the organization.

Passion for Seniors – Feels strongly about working with the senior population. Has a drive to go above and beyond for seniors. Typically, this comes from a personal experience or prior work experience in a senior citizen setting.

Integrity and Trust – Does what they say they will do, does not take the easy road, and does not misrepresent themselves for personal gain. Always does the right thing, even when it does not benefit themselves directly.

Research grant opportunities and appropriate matches
